title: Primary 3 Equivalent Fractions
seo_title: P3 Equivalent Fractions Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Equivalent fractions; simplest form; comparing and ordering unlike fractions (denominators not exceeding 12); writing an equivalent fraction given the numerator or denominator
meta_desc: Free P3 maths practice: equivalent fractions with fraction bars, simplest form, missing numbers and comparing fractions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
body_html:
What are equivalent fractions?

Equivalent fractions show the same amount. They have different numerators and denominators. Look at the three bars. They are the same length, and the shaded parts are the same length too.

A fraction wall helps you see more equivalent fractions.

Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number

To find an equivalent fraction, multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. You can also divide them both by the same number.

Example

Find a fraction equal to 23 with denominator 12.

3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8.

Answer: 23 = 812

Example

35 = 6?

3 × 2 = 6, so multiply the denominator by 2 too: 5 × 2 = 10.

Answer: 35 = 610

Simplest form

A fraction is in simplest form when 1 is the only number that divides both the numerator and the denominator. Divide them both by the biggest number you can.

FractionDivide both bySimplest form
68234
69323
812423

Comparing and ordering fractions

If the numerators are both 1, the fraction with the smaller denominator is greater. A whole cut into 4 parts has bigger parts than a whole cut into 8 parts.

For other fractions, write them with the same denominator first. Then compare the numerators.

Example

Which is greater, 34 or 58?

34 = 68. 6 eighths is more than 5 eighths.

Answer: 34

Example

Arrange 12, 38, 34 from the smallest to the greatest.

In eighths: 48, 38, 68. Order the numerators: 3, 4, 6.

Answer: 38, 12, 34

Word problems: draw a model

Draw a bar and cut it into equal units. The denominator tells you how many units.

Example

Mrs Ng cut a cake into 12 equal pieces. Her family ate 34 of it. How many pieces did they eat?

4 units = 12 pieces. 1 unit = 3 pieces. 3 units = 9 pieces.

Answer: 9 pieces

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
13 = 24 (adding 1 to the top and bottom)Multiply both by the same number: 13 = 26
18 > 14 (because 8 > 4)More parts means smaller parts: 18 < 14
812 = 46 (not fully simplified)Keep dividing: 46 = 23
25 = 45 (multiplying only the numerator)Multiply the denominator too: 25 = 410

faq.q: What is taught in P3 fractions?
faq.a: In Primary 3, students learn equivalent fractions, write fractions in simplest form, and compare and order fractions with different denominators up to 12. They also add and subtract simple fractions within 1 whole.

faq.q: How do I explain equivalent fractions to my child?
faq.a: Show two strips of paper of the same length: fold one into halves and the other into quarters. 1 half covers the same length as 2 quarters, so 1/2 = 2/4. To find more, multiply the top and bottom by the same number.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with equivalent fractions?
faq.a: Adding the same number to the top and bottom, as in 1/3 = 2/4. This changes the amount. Multiply instead: 1/3 = 2/6.

faq.q: Is equivalent fractions in the MOE syllabus for Primary 3?
faq.a: Yes. Equivalent fractions, simplest form, and comparing and ordering fractions are part of Fractions in the Primary 3 Standard Mathematics syllabus (MOE 2021). In Primary 4, students go on to mixed numbers and improper fractions.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The top bar shows 12. What fraction of the bottom bar is shaded?
items.e: The bottom bar has 6 equal parts and 3 of them are shaded, so it shows 36. The shaded parts are the same length, so 12 = 36.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The top bar shows 13. What fraction of the bottom bar is shaded?
items.e: The bottom bar has 6 equal parts and 2 of them are shaded, so it shows 26. The shaded parts are the same length, so 13 = 26.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The top bar shows 34. What fraction of the bottom bar is shaded?
items.e: The bottom bar has 8 equal parts and 6 of them are shaded, so it shows 68. The shaded parts are the same length, so 34 = 68.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The top bar shows 23. What fraction of the bottom bar is shaded?
items.e: The bottom bar has 12 equal parts and 8 of them are shaded, so it shows 812. The shaded parts are the same length, so 23 = 812.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The bottom bar has 8 equal parts. How many parts must be shaded to show a fraction equal to 12?
items.e: Each part of the top bar is cut into 4 small parts (2 × 4 = 8). 1 shaded part × 4 = 4. So 12 = 48. Shade 4 parts.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The bottom bar has 9 equal parts. How many parts must be shaded to show a fraction equal to 23?
items.e: Each part of the top bar is cut into 3 small parts (3 × 3 = 9). 2 shaded parts × 3 = 6. So 23 = 69. Shade 6 parts.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The bottom bar has 10 equal parts. How many parts must be shaded to show a fraction equal to 35?
items.e: Each part of the top bar is cut into 2 small parts (5 × 2 = 10). 3 shaded parts × 2 = 6. So 35 = 610. Shade 6 parts.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The bottom bar has 8 equal parts. How many parts must be shaded to show a fraction equal to 14?
items.e: Each part of the top bar is cut into 2 small parts (4 × 2 = 8). 1 shaded part × 2 = 2. So 14 = 28. Shade 2 parts.

items.q: The two bars are the same length. The bottom bar has 12 equal parts. How many parts must be shaded to show a fraction equal to 56?
items.e: Each part of the top bar is cut into 2 small parts (6 × 2 = 12). 5 shaded parts × 2 = 10. So 56 = 1012. Shade 10 parts.

items.e: The first circle has 1 of 2 equal slices shaded: 12. The second circle has 4 of 8 slices shaded: 48. The same amount is shaded, so 12 = 48.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which bar shows a fraction equal to 23?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 23 by 2: 23 = 46. Bar D has 4 of 6 parts shaded, so it shows 46. The answer is D.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which bar shows a fraction equal to 14?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 14 by 2: 14 = 28. Bar B has 2 of 8 parts shaded, so it shows 28. The answer is B.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which bar shows a fraction equal to 35?

items.q: Use the fraction wall. Which fraction is equal to 34?
items.e: Each quarter is as long as 2 eighths. So 3 quarters are as long as 6 eighths: 34 = 68.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. Which fraction is equal to 23?
items.e: Each third is as long as 4 twelfths. So 2 thirds are as long as 8 twelfths: 23 = 812.

sets.title: Multiply or divide the numerator and denominator

items.q: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 12 by 3. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 3: 1 × 3 = 3 and 2 × 3 = 6. So 12 = 36.

items.q: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 35 by 2. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 2: 3 × 2 = 6 and 5 × 2 = 10. So 35 = 610.

items.q: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 23 by 4. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 4: 2 × 4 = 8 and 3 × 4 = 12. So 23 = 812.

items.q: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 34 by 3. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12. So 34 = 912.

items.q: Multiply the numerator and the denominator of 16 by 2. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 2: 1 × 2 = 2 and 6 × 2 = 12. So 16 = 212.

items.q: Divide the numerator and the denominator of 68 by 2. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So 68 = 34.

items.q: Divide the numerator and the denominator of 812 by 4. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 4: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 812 = 23.

items.q: Divide the numerator and the denominator of 69 by 3. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 3: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. So 69 = 23.

items.q: Divide the numerator and the denominator of 412 by 4. Which fraction do you get?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 4: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. So 412 = 13.

items.q: To write 23 in twelfths, you multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. What is the number?
items.e: The denominator must change from 3 to 12. 3 × 4 = 12, so the number is 4. 23 = 812.

items.q: To write 34 in eighths, you multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. What is the number?
items.e: The denominator must change from 4 to 8. 4 × 2 = 8, so the number is 2. 34 = 68.

items.q: To write 15 in tenths, you multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number. What is the number?
items.e: The denominator must change from 5 to 10. 5 × 2 = 10, so the number is 2. 15 = 210.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 34?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 2: 3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 2 = 8. So 34 = 68.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 25?
items.e: Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 2: 2 × 2 = 4 and 5 × 2 = 10. So 25 = 410.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 46?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 6 ÷ 2 = 3. So 46 = 23.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 912?
items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator by 3: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 12 ÷ 3 = 4. So 912 = 34.

items.q: Siti wrote 13 = 24. What mistake did she make?
c: She added 1 to the top and bottom
items.e: Adding the same number to the top and bottom does not give an equal fraction. 13 = 412, but 24 = 612, which is bigger. Multiply instead: 13 = 26.

items.q: Hui Min wrote 25 = 45. What mistake did she make?
c: She added 2 to the top and bottom
items.e: Hui Min multiplied only the numerator, so the parts did not change: 45 is twice 25. Multiply the denominator too: 25 = 410.

items.e: Divide the numerator and the denominator of 312 by 3: 14. So 14 and 312 are equivalent.

items.q: The bar shows 68. The thick lines put the parts into groups of 2. What is 68 in simplest form?
items.e: There are 4 groups and 3 of them are shaded. 6 and 8 can both be divided by 2. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. 1 is the only number that divides both 3 and 4, so 34 is in simplest form. 68 = 34.

items.q: The bar shows 69. The thick lines put the parts into groups of 3. What is 69 in simplest form?
items.e: There are 3 groups and 2 of them are shaded. 6 and 9 can both be divided by 3. 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. 1 is the only number that divides both 2 and 3, so 23 is in simplest form. 69 = 23.

items.q: Write 24 in its simplest form.
items.e: 2 and 4 can both be divided by 2. 2 ÷ 2 = 1 and 4 ÷ 2 = 2. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 2, so 12 is in simplest form. 24 = 12.

items.q: Write 36 in its simplest form.
items.e: 3 and 6 can both be divided by 3. 3 ÷ 3 = 1 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 2, so 12 is in simplest form. 36 = 12.

items.q: Write 28 in its simplest form.
items.e: 2 and 8 can both be divided by 2. 2 ÷ 2 = 1 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 4, so 14 is in simplest form. 28 = 14.

items.q: Write 510 in its simplest form.
items.e: 5 and 10 can both be divided by 5. 5 ÷ 5 = 1 and 10 ÷ 5 = 2. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 2, so 12 is in simplest form. 510 = 12.

items.q: Write 39 in its simplest form.
items.e: 3 and 9 can both be divided by 3. 3 ÷ 3 = 1 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 3, so 13 is in simplest form. 39 = 13.

items.q: Write 48 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 and 8 can both be divided by 4. 4 ÷ 4 = 1 and 8 ÷ 4 = 2. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 2, so 12 is in simplest form. 48 = 12.

items.q: Write 68 in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 and 8 can both be divided by 2. 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and 8 ÷ 2 = 4. 1 is the only number that divides both 3 and 4, so 34 is in simplest form. 68 = 34.

items.q: Write 210 in its simplest form.
items.e: 2 and 10 can both be divided by 2. 2 ÷ 2 = 1 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. 1 is the only number that divides both 1 and 5, so 15 is in simplest form. 210 = 15.

items.q: Write 410 in its simplest form.
items.e: 4 and 10 can both be divided by 2. 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. 1 is the only number that divides both 2 and 5, so 25 is in simplest form. 410 = 25.

items.q: Write 69 in its simplest form.
items.e: 6 and 9 can both be divided by 3. 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 9 ÷ 3 = 3. 1 is the only number that divides both 2 and 3, so 23 is in simplest form. 69 = 23.

items.q: Write 812 in its simplest form.
items.e: 8 and 12 can both be divided by 4. 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. 1 is the only number that divides both 2 and 3, so 23 is in simplest form. 812 = 23.

items.q: Write 612 in its simplest form.

items.q: Write 1012 in its simplest form.
items.e: 10 and 12 can both be divided by 2. 10 ÷ 2 = 5 and 12 ÷ 2 = 6. 1 is the only number that divides both 5 and 6, so 56 is in simplest form. 1012 = 56.

items.q: Which fraction is in its simplest form?
items.e: 38: 1 is the only number that divides both 3 and 8, so it is in simplest form. 26 = 13. 410 = 25. 69 = 23. The answer is 38.

items.q: Only one of these fractions is in simplest form. Which one?

items.q: To write 812 in simplest form in one step, what is the biggest number you can divide 8 and 12 by?
items.e: 2 divides both 8 and 12, but 4 is bigger and also divides both: 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. 6 does not divide 8, and 8 does not divide 12. The answer is 4, so 812 = 23.

items.e: 46 is equal to 812, but 4 and 6 can both still be divided by 2: 46 = 23. Keep dividing until 1 is the only number that divides both.

items.q: All the bars are the same length. Which fraction is the smallest?
items.e: The more equal parts a whole is cut into, the smaller each part is. The bar cut into 8 parts has the shortest shaded part. The answer is 18.

items.q: On Sports Day, Ryan ran 34 km, Chloe ran 58 km, Arjun ran 12 km and Priya ran 38 km. Who ran the furthest?
items.e: Write the distances in eighths: 34 = 68, 12 = 48. Compare the numerators: 6, 5, 4 and 3. Ryan ran the furthest.

items.q: Mrs Lim has four ribbons. The red ribbon is 23 m long, the blue ribbon is 56 m long, the green ribbon is 712 m long and the yellow ribbon is 34 m long. Which ribbon is the shortest?
items.e: Write the lengths in twelfths: 23 = 812, 56 = 1012, 34 = 912. Compare the numerators: 8, 10, 7 and 9. 7 is the smallest, so the green ribbon is the shortest.

items.q: Mei Ling, Kumar, Devi and Ethan have water bottles of the same size. Mei Ling’s bottle is 34 full, Kumar’s is 23 full, Devi’s is 512 full and Ethan’s is 12 full. Whose bottle has the most water?
items.e: The bottles are the same size. Write the fractions in twelfths: 34 = 912, 23 = 812, 12 = 612. Compare the numerators: 9, 8, 5 and 6. Mei Ling has the most water.

items.q: Kavya read 58 of a storybook. Raju read 34 of the same storybook. Who read more?
c: Raju, because 34 = 68
items.e: Write 34 in eighths: 68. Raju read 68 and Kavya read 58. 6 > 5, so Raju read more. You cannot compare 5 and 3 when the parts are different sizes.

items.q: Siti ate 28 of a pizza. Jun Jie ate 14 of another pizza of the same size. Which is true?
items.e: Siti ate 28. Write Jun Jie’s 14 in eighths: 28. 28 = 14, so they ate the same amount.

items.q: Mrs Ng cut a pandan cake into 12 equal pieces. Her family ate 34 of the cake. How many pieces did they eat?
items.e: Draw a model of 4 units for quarters. 4 units = 12 pieces, so 1 unit = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 pieces. 3 units = 3 × 3 = 9 pieces. So 34 = 912.

items.q: Xin Yi folded a paper strip into equal parts. She coloured 4 parts. The coloured parts are 13 of the strip. How many equal parts are there?
items.e: Draw a model of 3 units for thirds. 1 unit = 4 parts. 3 units = 3 × 4 = 12 parts. So 13 = 412.

items.q:
Zhi Hao had a bar of chocolate with 10 equal pieces. He gave 4 pieces to his sister. What fraction of the bar did he give away?
Give your answer in its simplest form.
items.e: He gave away 4 of the 10 pieces: 410. 4 and 10 can both be divided by 2. 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 10 ÷ 2 = 5. 1 is the only number that divides both 2 and 5, so 25 is in simplest form. 410 = 25.
